issues.description: Extraction unconditionally requires data/stories/manifest.json and story files, but the repo contains no story data, so the documented demo and integration test fail.
The tiny end-to-end test depends on missing external story fixtures instead of self-contained test data or generated tiny data.
The documented tiny CPU demo commands are not reproducible from a fresh checkout because required data files are absent.
Checked-in outputs reference a source story manifest that is not present in the repository, making artifacts stale and unreproducible.
stories_dir is resolved relative to the caller's current working directory instead of the config file location, so commands break when run outside the repo root.
A PCA variance threshold of 0 is accepted but still returns one component, causing unintended projection when zero neutral-PC removal should mean none.
Vector artifacts are loaded without validating backend, layer count, d_model, or emotion compatibility before matrix operations.
Preference steering loads vector artifacts without compatibility checks, so using tiny vectors with the HF backend fails later with cryptic shape errors.
Validation does not handle the case where configured emotions have no built-in scenarios, leading to empty stacks or NaN summary metrics.
HF residual activation calls do not set truncation or max_length, so long stories can exceed the model context window and crash.
The HF backend loads the full model and then moves it to one device, ignoring device_map-style loading and making the default Gemma run fragile on limited hardware.
HF preference scoring assumes the first token of ' good' and ' bad' is a stable preference signal, which is tokenizer/model fragile and untested.
Tiny emotion matching uses substring counts, so unrelated words can accidentally contribute emotion signal.
Test configuration is minimal and does not enforce coverage, warnings-as-errors, or any tests for the HF backend path.
